chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Which hour do you prefer for us to depart from Mina (for 'Arafat/Muzdalifah)?' He said: 'A little before the sun rises, that is the most beloved of the hours to me.' I said: 'And if I stay until the sun rises?' He said: 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm / it is permissible
key_terms.نُفِيضَ: to depart or set out (from a place)

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to leave Muzdalifah during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the preference for departing Muzdalifah before sunrise is highlighted as the ideal practice (mustahabb), reflecting the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams. However, the Imam’s affirmation that staying until sunrise is 'not bad' (laysa bi-ba's) establishes the flexibility and validity of the later time, accommodating the needs of pilgrims. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the temporal boundaries of the Muzdalifah rite, balancing spiritual diligence with practical ease.
